entities.summary: The Hindu Shahis, also referred to as the Kabul Shahis and Uḍi Śāhis, were a dynasty established between 843 CE and 1026 CE. Enduring multiple waves of conquests for nearly two centuries, the western frontiers of their core territory comprised the regions of Gandhara and Kabulistan in contemporary Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and eastern Afghanistan, while eastern frontiers expanded to the Sutlej River, encompassing the regions of Punjab and the Kangra Valley in contemporary Punjab, Pakistan, Punjab, India, and Himachal Pradesh.
